p0.original: 关键问题：我们如何提取记忆
p0.en: Question: How do we extract memories?

p2.original: 无论是内隐记忆还是外显记忆，能否成功地将其提取都取决于它们如何被编码和被提示。
p2.en: Whether it is hidden or visible, its successful extraction depends on how well they are coded and activated.

p3.original: 在提取记忆的过程中，记忆会耍一些出人意料的花招。其中一个就是你可能会提取出一些你不知道自己拥有的记忆，这告诉我们一些记忆可以在完全没有意识参与的情况下被成功编码和存储。另一个奇事是我们会对自己的回忆过于自信，就像我们在“闪光灯记忆”部分看到的那样。这一学习阶段的核心概念总结记忆提取的过程如下：
p3.en: In the process of extracting memories, memory can play some surprising tricks. One of them is that you might extract memories that you don't know about, which tells us that some memories can be coded and stored without any conscious involvement. Another strange thing is that we'll be too confident in our memories, as we've seen in the flashlight memory section. The process of extracting the core concepts from this learning phase is as follows:

p4.original: 无论是内隐记忆还是外显记忆，能否成功地将其提取都取决于它们如何被编码和被提示。
p4.en: Whether it is hidden or visible, its successful extraction depends on how well they are coded and activated.

p6.original: 5.5 评估提取线索是否有助于记忆。
p6.en: 5.5 Assessment of whether extraction leads are useful for memory.

p9.original: 评估提取线索是否有助于记忆。
p9.en: Assesses whether extraction leads can help memory.

p10.original: 我们从一个奇怪的问题开始这一学习阶段的内容：你总能意识到自己的记忆吗？对于H.M.来说，答案是否定的：尽管他对动作任务有正常的程序性记忆，但他不记得自己学习过这些技能，甚至不知道自己会这些技能。但是，即使不像H.M.那样有脑损伤，你依然无法察觉到自己的一些记忆。正常人的记忆也存在失联的信息孤岛。一百多年来，心理学家已经意识到那些没有记忆缺陷的人也可以在不知道自己知道的情况下知道一些事情。心理学家丹尼尔·沙克特（Daniel Schacter）把这种记忆称为内隐记忆（implicit memory）：那些在你没有完全意识到的情况下可以影响你的行为的记忆（1992，1996）。相比之下，外显记忆（explicit memory）则需要意识参与。
p10.en: We begin this learning phase with a strange question: can you always be aware of your memory? For H.M., the answer is no: although he has a normal procedural memory of mobility tasks, he does not remember learning these skills, even knowing that he does. But even if you don't have brain damage like H.M., you still can't feel some of your memories. There is also a missing information island in the memory of normal people. For more than a century, psychologists have realized that those without memory impairments can also know something without knowing what they know. The psychologist Daniel Schacter described this memory as hidden memory: memories that can influence your behaviour if you are not fully aware (1992, 1996). In contrast, the epitome (explicit memory) requires conscious participation.

p11.original: 通常，程序性记忆都是内隐记忆，例如，高尔夫球手无须考虑身体如何移动也记得如何挥杆。但是内隐记忆并不局限于程序性记忆，外显记忆也不等同于陈述性记忆。你的语义记忆中存储的信息既可以是外显的（如记住你为准备考试而复习的材料），也可以是内隐的（如知道你上心理学课的那栋建筑的颜色）。判断记忆是内隐还是外显的一般规律是这样的：如果一段记忆能够在无意识的情况下影响人的行为或心理过程，那么它就是内隐的。另外，在存储和提取过程中，外显记忆总有意识参与。
p11.en: Generally, procedural memory is hidden, for example, when golfers do not have to consider how their bodies move or how to swing. But hidden memory is not limited to procedural memory, nor is outward memory equivalent to narrative memory. The information stored in your semantic memory can be either visible (e.g. remembering the material you studied to prepare for the exam) or hidden (e.g. the color of the building where you took psychology classes). Whether memory is hidden or visible is the general rule: if a memory can influence a person's behaviour or psychological processes without being conscious, it is hidden. In addition, during storage and extraction processes, the explicit memory is always consciously involved.

p12.original: 在一系列引人注目的研究中，斯科特克和他的同事们（Skotko et al.，2004）发现，H.M.可以通过内隐通路习得一些新的语义材料，即使他不知道自己已经学习过这些材料。为了做到这一点，斯科特克的团队使用H.M.最喜欢的消遣方式——填字游戏。他们设计了能够帮助H.M.将新信息与他在做手术之前已经掌握的知识联系起来的填字游戏。例如，H.M.的确知道小儿麻痹症是一种可怕的疾病，但由于小儿麻痹症疫苗是在他手术后才被发明出来的，所以他对此一无所知。然而，通过在5天的时间里完成一种经特殊设计的填字游戏，H.M.学会了对“Salk疫苗能成功治疗儿童期疾病”这个题目做出正确的反应。同样，他还知道了被暗杀的约翰·肯尼迪总统（President John Kennedy）的妻子杰奎琳·肯尼迪（Jacqueline Kennedy）后来成了杰奎琳·奥纳西斯（Jacqueline Onassis）。这种技术表明，H.M.的记忆问题主要存在于外显记忆，而不是语义记忆中。
p12.en: In a series of remarkable studies, Skotko et al., 2004 found that H.M. could learn some new semantic material through a hidden path, even though he did not know that he had learned it. To do this, Scott's team uses H.M.'s favorite play-word puzzle. They designed crossword games that helped H.M. to link new information to knowledge that he had acquired before the operation. For example, H.M. did know that polio was a terrible disease, but he was unaware of it because the polio vaccine had been invented after his surgery. However, by completing a specially designed crossword puzzle in five days, H.M. learned to respond correctly to the topic “Salk vaccines can successfully treat childhood diseases”. Similarly, he was aware that Jacqueline Kennedy, the wife of President John Kennedy, had subsequently become Jacqueline Onassis. This technology suggests that the memory problems of H.M. are mainly in visible rather than semantic memory.

p14.original: 内隐记忆和外显记忆都需要良好的线索以准确地提取信息。如果你曾经用过谷歌浏览器或者其他的搜索引擎，那么你肯定对这类线索有一定的了解：当你输入一个糟糕的搜索词时，你可能会一无所获，或者得到一些网络垃圾。长时记忆的工作原理与搜索引擎大致相同，成功的搜索需要依赖于良好的心理提取线索（retrieval cue）。有时，重新激活一段长期深埋在记忆中的经历，所需的唯一提取线索可能是某种气味。例如，新鲜出炉的饼干的香气会让你联想到去奶奶家的经历。在其他时候，提取线索也可能是一种情绪。例如，一个与抑郁症抗争的人会陷入抑郁记忆的旋涡中。在本章开头提到的罗斯的故事中，他梦到的某些东西可能成了提取他早已遗忘的那段记忆的线索。
p14.en: Both hidden and visible memories require good leads to extract information accurately. If you've used Google Browser or any other search engine, you must have some idea of this clue: when you enter a bad search word, you might have nothing or some Internet trash. The work of long-term memory is roughly the same as that of the search engine, and successful search requires good psychological extraction (retrievable cue). Sometimes, the only extraction leads that are needed to reactivate a long, deep memory experience may be some kind of scent. For example, the smell of fresh cookies brings you back to Grandma's house. At other times, extraction of clues can also be an emotional phenomenon. For example, a person who struggles with depression is caught in the vortex of depression memory. In the story of Ross, mentioned at the beginning of this chapter, something he dreamed of could become a clue to the memory he had forgotten for a long time.

p15.original: 一些记忆——尤其是语义记忆——不是很容易被线索提示。例如，在考试中，如果一个问题的说法与你学习时在脑海中所构建的信息不匹配，那么当你看到这个问题时，你的脑海里可能就会一片空白。换句话说，如果这个问题不是一个很好的提取线索，你可能就无法成功地提取相关记忆。一般来说，提取线索是否有效，取决于所寻找的记忆类型以及包含该记忆的联结网络。从中我们能获得什么启示呢？你建立的联结网络越广泛，成功提取信息的机会就越大。让我们看看如何利用这些信息来提高你的记忆提取能力。
p15.en: Some memories — especially semantic memories — are not easy to be hinted at. For example, if, in the examination, the statement of an issue does not match the information that you built in your mind when you studied, then when you see it, your mind may be blank. In other words, if this problem is not a good extraction trail, you may not be able to successfully extract the relevant memories. In general, the effectiveness of extracting leads depends on the type of memory sought and the network of connections containing that memory. And what do we get from it? The more extensive the network you have established, the greater the chances of successfully extracting information. Let's see how this information can be used to improve your memory extraction.

p16.original: 有意义组织的重要性 确保记忆能够准确提取的最好方法，就是在编码过程中为信息赋予意义。这意味着在第一次遇到某个新信息时，你必须将其与你已经知道的知识联系起来。有时候准确地记住所有细节很重要（如记住一个数学公式），而在其他一些时候，重要的是记住信息的要点。当你试图记住这些信息的要点时，为这些概念和观点想出个人化的例子就十分重要。我们将这一过程称为精细复述。通过精细复述来编码许多这样的连接会给你提供更多的通达这些信息的方式，就像人们可以从多条道路到达一个城镇一样。（你是否养成了在看到章节概念时就与自身的例子建立联系的习惯呢？）
p16.en: The best way to ensure that memory can be accurately extracted is to give meaning to information in the coding process. This means that when you first encounter a new message, you have to link it to the knowledge you already know. Sometimes it is important to remember all the details accurately (e.g. a mathematical formula), while in other cases it is important to remember the main points of the information. When you try to remember the main points of this information, it is important to think of individualized examples of these concepts and perspectives. We call this process a fine recapitulation. Encoding many of these connections by recapitulating them will give you more access to this information, just as people can reach a town from multiple roads. (Do you have the habit of linking your own example when you look at the concept of a chapter? I don't think so.

p17.original: 通过启动提取内隐记忆 披头士（Beatle）乐队前成员乔治·哈里森（George Harrison）因一段有关内隐记忆的巧合而被送上法庭（Schacter，1996）。雪纺（Clifons）乐队的律师称，哈里森的歌曲《我亲爱的上帝》（My Sweet Lord）中使用的旋律与雪纺乐队的经典歌曲《他很好》（He's So Fine）中的旋律几乎完全一样。哈里森否认自己故意剽窃这首歌曲的旋律，但他承认在创作自己的曲子之前听过雪纺乐队的歌曲。法庭对此表示认同，他们认为哈里森的借用是“潜意识记忆”的产物。在最近的另一个案件中，法瑞尔·威廉姆斯（Pharrell Williams）承认马文·盖伊（Marvin Gaye）对其音乐创作有一定的影响，但断然否认在参与创作歌曲《模糊界限》（Blurred Lines）时剽窃了盖伊的《必须放弃》（Got To Give It Up）中的音乐元素。在2015年的这个案件中，法院并没有因威廉姆斯的陈述而动摇，而是判威廉姆斯向盖伊的后人支付数百万美元的赔偿金。两起案件非常相似，但最终判决结果却不同，这表明内隐记忆的界限是模糊的。日常生活中充满了与之相似的经历。你可能向朋友提出了一个想法，但被他拒绝了。几周后，你的朋友会激动地向你提出同样的想法，好像这是一个全新的想法一样。
p17.en: George Harrison, a former member of the Beatle band, was brought to court for a coincidence about the hidden memory (Schacter, 1996). The lawyer for the Cliftons claimed that Harrison's song My Sweet Lord used the same melody as the classic song of the Snow Wing, He's So Fine. Harrison denied that he deliberately stole the melody of the song, but he admitted to having heard the song of the Snow Roll before he created his own song. The Tribunal agreed, and they considered Harrison's borrowing to be the product of “subconscious memory”. In another recent case, the Pharmall Williams acknowledged that Marvin Gaye had had some influence on his music creation, but categorically denied the theft of the music element in Got To Give It Up when he was involved in the creation of the song Bhurred Lines. In the 2015 case, the Court did not waver from Williams ' statements, but instead sentenced Williams to pay millions of dollars in damages to the late Guy. The two cases were very similar, but the final verdict was different, suggesting that the boundaries of hidden memory were blurred. Every day is filled with similar experiences. You may have put a thought into your friend, but he turned it down. In a few weeks, your friends will be excited to offer you the same idea, as if it were an entirely new one.

p18.original: 在现实生活中，我们很难说出是什么因素促使内隐记忆浮出水面。然而，心理学家已经在实验室中开发出了“启动”内隐记忆的方法（Schacter，1996）。例如，想象你自愿参加了一个记忆实验。首先，你有几秒的时间浏览如下的单词列表：
p18.en: In real life, it is difficult to tell what causes hidden memories to surface. However, psychologists have developed a method of “starting” hidden memories in laboratories (Schacter, 1996). For example, imagine you volunteered for a memory experiment. First of all, you have a few seconds to browse through the following list of words:

p20.original: 然后，一小时后，实验人员会让你看另一个单词列表：twilight，assassin，dinosaur，mystery。并且要求你指出其中是否有你在之前的列表中看到的词汇。这个任务对你来说很容易。但是在这之后，实验人员会给你看一些缺少字母的单词并让你填空：
p20.en: Then, in an hour, the experimenter will show you another word list: twilight, asssin, diosaur, Mystery. And I ask you to indicate if you have any of the words you saw in the previous list. This mission is easy for you. But after that, the lab will show you some words that are missing letters and make you empty:

p22.original: 当你填空时，“octopus”（章鱼）和“climate”（气候）两个答案可能很快就浮现在了你的脑海中。但是，你在填写另两个词“chipmunk”（花栗鼠）和“bogeyman”（妖怪）时可能就没那么容易了。这种差异是由启动（priming）造成的，启动是在无意识的情况下提供线索激发记忆的过程。因为你已经被下面两个词启动了：“octopus”和“climate”。所以，与没有被启动的词相比，它们会更容易在你的意识中“冒出来”。
p22.en: When you fill out, the answers to "octopus" and "climate" may soon be in your mind. But you might not be that easy to fill in the other two words, "chipmunk" and "bogeyman". This difference is caused by a start-up (priming) process that provides clues to stimulate memory in an unconscious situation. Because you've already started with the following two words: "octopus" and "climate." So, they are easier to “come out” in your mind than if they were not activated.

p23.original: 通过回忆和再认提取外显记忆 你可以通过两种主要线索提示外显记忆。一种是论述题测验中用到的提取线索；另一种是选择题测验中用到的线索。
p23.en: And by reminiscing and re-recognizing, you can hint through two main clues to the re-emergence. One is the extraction thread used in the discussion quiz; The other is the thread used in the selection test.

p24.original: 1. 论述题测验要求回答者用最少的线索回忆（recall）或提取一段记忆。也就是说，在论述题测验中，你必须在问题给出较少线索的情况下几乎完全凭借自己的记忆写出答案。例如，回答“外显记忆的两种提示方式是什么”这一问题。
p24.en: 1. The question-and-answer test requires the respondent to use the minimum lead memory or to extract a memory. That is to say, in the talking quiz, you have to write the answer almost entirely on your own memory, with fewer clues. For example, the answer to the question “What are the two hints of an apparent memory”.

p25.original: 2. 再认（recognition）是人们完成选择题时所需要用到的记忆提取方法。在一个再认任务中，你只需要判断之前是否见过与题目中线索类似的刺激。通常，再认任务比回忆任务的要求更低，因为再认任务提供的线索更完整。
p25.en: Reconfirmation (recognition) is the method of extraction of memory that people need to use to complete their selection. In a recertification mission, you just have to judge whether you have seen a similar stimulus to the clues in the subject. Often, the re-recognition mission is less demanding than the recall mission, as it provides more complete clues.

p26.original: 当警察要求目击者从一排人中指认嫌疑人时，他们使用的就是再认的方法。目击者只需要将记忆中的图像（罪犯的长相）与当前的刺激（队列中的嫌疑人）进行匹配即可。那么与之对应的回忆任务是怎样的呢？目击者完全回忆起嫌疑人的面部特征，并与警察画师一起画出嫌疑人的外貌。
p26.en: When witnesses were asked by the police to identify suspects from a platoon, they used the method of re-identification. Witnesses simply need to match the images in their memories (the faces of the criminals) with the current stimulus (the suspects in the queue). So what's the task of remembering it? Eyewitnesses fully recalled the features of the suspect's face and, together with the police painter, painted the suspect's appearance.

p27.original: 当然，把一个刺激再认出来并不是只需找出与当前环境相匹配的刺激即可。当我们在做选择题时常会遇到这样的问题，即题目中提供的几个选项都是我们学过的概念，但只有一个概念适用于当前特定的问题。类似地，如果警方向目击者出示了一个或多个嫌疑人被逮捕时的面部照片，目击者也可能会误将其中的一名嫌疑人指认为罪犯。在这种情况下，因为目击者只是基于疑犯被逮捕时的照片而不是在真实犯罪情境中辨认罪犯，他们可能会将嫌疑人误认为是罪犯（Weiner et al.，2003）。因此，尽管再认通常能激活比回忆更多的记忆，但它也更可能产生误报的现象，或者如在本例中产生的错误记忆。通过使用本章提到的一些技巧，你可以帮助自己在考试中避免这类错误，从而更有效地记住你想要学习的内容。
p27.en: Of course, recognizing a stimulus is not just about finding a stimulus that matches the current environment. When we make choices, we often encounter the problem that several of the options provided in the subject are concepts that we have learned, but only one applies to specific issues at the present time. Similarly, if the police showed witnesses a photograph of one or more suspects in the face at the time of their arrest, witnesses might have mistakenly identified one of them as the perpetrator. In such cases, since witnesses are based only on photographs of the suspect at the time of his arrest and not on the identification of the offender in the context of a real criminal situation, they may mistakenly regard the suspect as a criminal (Weiner et al., 2003). Thus, while re-recognition usually activates more memories than memories, it can also lead to more misreporting or, as in this case, to false memories. By using some of the techniques mentioned in this chapter, you can help yourself avoid such errors in the examination, so as to remember more effectively what you want to learn.

p28.original: 5.5.2 其他影响记忆提取的因素

p29.original: 我们已经知道，从外显的陈述性记忆中提取信息的能力取决于信息是否经过编码和精细加工而获得了意义。警觉、应激水平、药物和一般知识也会影响记忆的提取，当你了解了这个知识点时可能并不会感到惊讶。然而，接下来的内容则鲜为人知，它们与你编码和记忆时所处的背景（context）有关。
p29.en: As we already know, the ability to extract information from an apparent narrative memory depends on whether the information is meaningful through coding and fine processing. Alerting, stress levels, drugs and general knowledge can also affect the extraction of memories, and it may not surprise you when you learn about this point of knowledge. However, the next elements are rarely known, and they relate to the context in which you code and remember.

p30.original: 编码特异性 提取线索与信息被编码的形式越匹配，就越能通过线索提取适当的记忆。例如，也许你在超市见到了你的心理学教授，但是你需要一点时间来认出她或他是谁，因为你所处的背景并没有提示你想到“心理学教授”的相关信息。另外，和儿时的朋友聊天可能会让你想起许多你多年没有回忆起的往事。这两种经历都说明了编码特异性原则（encoding specificity principle），即成功的回忆取决于你的提取线索与记忆编码时存在的线索的匹配程度。
p30.en: And the more you get the clues and the more the information is coded, the more you get the proper memory. For example, you may have seen your professor of psychology at the supermarket, but you need a little time to recognize her or who he is, because your background does not remind you of the relevant information about the “mentor of psychology”. Besides, talking to your childhood friends may remind you of a lot of things you haven't remembered for years. Both experiences illustrate the principle of coding specificity, that is, successful memories depend on the match between your extraction leads and the clues that exist when the memory code is coded.

p31.original: 所以，在备考的过程中，你能做的一件重要的事情就是预测考试中可能出现的提取线索，并围绕这些可能出现的线索组织你的复习内容。那些仅仅阅读复习材料，并希望能以此取得好成绩的学生往往无法获得预期的结果。事实上，这是一个很普遍的问题，心理学家罗伯特·比约克（Bjork，2000）建议教师在课程中引入“适当的困难”（desirable difficulties），从而鼓励学生以多种方式对材料进行编码。什么是适当的困难？比约克认为，通过给学生分配任务，要求他们以多种不同的方式与学习材料进行交互，如做项目、写论文、解决问题和进行课堂演示等。教授帮助学生建立一个记忆内容嵌入其中的更大的联结网络，联结越多，越容易成为线索帮助回忆。如果你的教授没有这样做，你能做些什么来为你正在学习的概念建立更多联结呢？
p31.en: So, one important thing you can do in preparing for the examination is predicting what clues may be drawn from the examination and organizing your review around these possible clues. Those who read only the review materials and hope to achieve good results are often unable to achieve the desired results. In fact, this is a very common problem, and the psychologist Robert Bjork, 2000 has recommended that teachers introduce “appropriate difficulties” into the curriculum, thereby encouraging students to codify materials in a variety of ways. What's the proper difficulty? By assigning tasks to students, Björk believes, students are required to interact with learning materials in a variety of ways, such as doing projects, writing papers, solving problems and conducting classroom presentations. The professor helps students to build a larger network of connections embedded in the memory content, the more connected they are, the easier it is to be a clue to the memory. If your professor has not done so, what can you do to build more links to the concept you are learning?

p32.original: 心境和记忆 信息加工不仅涉及事实和事件，也涉及情绪和心境。我们用“感觉整个世界很灰暗”[2]和“透过玫瑰色眼镜看世界”[3]这种说法来说明心境会影响我们对世界的感知。同样，我们的心境也会影响我们的记忆，这种现象被称为心境一致性记忆（mood-congruent memory）。如果你曾有过无法抑制自己大笑的经历，你就会知道欣快的心境是如何引发一个又一个搞笑的想法的。而在心境维度的另一个极端，抑郁的人经常报告他们所有的想法都有忧郁的一面。通过这种方式，抑郁的心境可以通过提取抑郁的记忆而持续存在（Sakaki，2007）。
p32.en: The heart and memory of information processing involves not only facts and events, but also emotions and hearts. We use the words “Impression of the whole world as gray”[2] and “Looking at the world through rose glasses”[3] to illustrate how our hearts affect our perception of the world. Likewise, our hearts will affect our memories, which are known as the memory of the moood-congruent memory. If you've ever had an experience of being unable to stop yourself laughing, you'll know how a happy heart has triggered one funny idea after another. And at the other extreme of the heart, depressed people often report that all their thoughts have a depressed side. In this way, depression can persist by extracting depression (Sakaki, 2007).

p33.original: 心境一致性记忆的研究并不只是出于实验室的好奇，这个现象对个人健康也有重要的影响。记忆研究人员戈登·鲍尔（Gordon Bower）曾说：“医生会根据你抱怨的内容和抱怨的多少来评估如何治疗你。”（McCarthy，1991）因为抑郁症患者很可能会强调他们的医学症状，所以他们接受的治疗可能与那些患有相同疾病但更乐观的人不同。鲍尔说，这意味着医生在决定诊断和疗程时，必须学会将患者的心理状态考虑在内。
p33.en: Research on the memory of consistency is not based solely on laboratory curiosity, but it also has an important impact on individual health. The memory researcher Gordon Bower once said, "Doctors will evaluate how to treat you based on the content of your complaints and how many complaints you complain. Because of the likelihood that depression patients will highlight their medical symptoms, they may be treated differently from those who suffer from the same disease but are more optimistic. According to Bauer, this means that doctors must learn to take into account the patient's mental state when deciding on the diagnosis and treatment process.

p34.original: 前瞻性记忆 记住在将来的某一时刻要做什么是最常见的记忆任务——例如，预约医生，和朋友共进午餐，或者在指定的日子倒垃圾等。心理学家将这些称为前瞻性记忆（prospective memory）。前瞻性记忆的问题——往往占日常生活中记忆问题的一多半（Crovitz & Daniel，1984）——轻则会造成轻度的不方便和尴尬，重则会导致恐怖的后果：
p34.en: Foresee memory, remember what is most common to remember at some point in the future -- for example, booking doctors, having lunch with friends, or dumping garbage on a given day. Psychologists refer to these as forward-looking memories. The problem of forward-looking memory, which often accounts for more than half of the problem of memory in everyday life (Crovitz & Daniel, 1984), can cause mild inconvenience and embarrassment, while heavy can lead to the consequences of terror:

p35.original: 一名男性在有了孩子后，他的日常安排发生了改变。一天，他忘记了要拐弯把孩子送到日托中心，而是按照以前的常规路线开车去大学上班。几小时后，在汽车后座上静静睡着的孩子不幸去世了（Einstein & McDaniel，2005）。
p35.en: After having a child, a man changed his day-to-day arrangements. One day, he forgot to turn the child to a day-care centre, and instead drove to university on the usual route. A few hours later, the child who fell asleep in the backseat of the car died in an unfortunate state (Einstein & McDaniel, 2005).

p36.original: 如此可怕的事情是怎么发生的呢？这名父亲可能在完成他预定的任务时分了心，从而陷入习惯性的常规日程中，就像每年都有父母会出现类似的情况一样。为了避免这种类型的记忆错误，专家建议人们创建一个提示线索，并把它放在某个你肯定会看到的地方。对于上述例子中的父亲来说，这可能意味着他应该把他的公文包放在后座上孩子的旁边，这样取公文包时他就能想起送孩子去日托中心。
p36.en: How did such a terrible thing happen? The father may have been distracted in the course of his scheduled tasks, and thus fall into a customary routine, as is the case each year when a similar situation occurs among parents. In order to avoid this type of memory error, experts suggest that people create a hint and place it somewhere you're sure to see. For the father in the above example, this may mean that he should place his briefcase next to the child in the back seat, so that when the briefcase is taken he can think about sending the child to the day care centre.

p37.original: 多任务处理是前瞻性记忆失败的主要原因（Dismukes，2012）。当我们同时处理多项任务时，如果这些任务不需要太多意识注意，我们似乎就能够处理好这些任务。然而，当需要把注意力集中在其中一项任务上时，我们的注意就会完全转离，甚至完全忘记其他任务。你是否经历过这种情况？
p37.en: Multitasking is the main cause of forward-looking memory failure (Dismukes, 2012). When we deal with multiple tasks simultaneously, it seems that if they do not require too much awareness, we can manage them. However, when attention needs to be focused on one of those tasks, our attention will be completely diverted and even forgotten about the others. Have you ever been through this?

p38.original: 前瞻性记忆影响我们生活的方方面面，从航空安全到个人健康。事实上，有五分之一的航空事故都可以归咎于前瞻性记忆的遗忘（Berman & Dismukes，2006）。例如，飞行员必须在起飞和降落前完成一套精心设计的操作程序，如果在这一过程中飞行员分心做其他事情，那么他可能就会忘记自己在这个过程中做到哪一步，从而遗漏一个重要的操作步骤。每天都需要服用药物的人被其他事情打断了早晨（或晚上）的例行服药程序，也会遇到同样的问题，他们可能不记得自己是否服用了药物，这增加了他们心脏病发作或死亡的风险（Nelson et al.，2006）。
p38.en: Forward-looking memories affect all aspects of our lives, from aviation security to personal health. Indeed, one fifth of aviation accidents can be attributed to the oblivion of forward-looking memories (Berman & Dismukes, 2006). For example, the pilot must complete a well-designed operating procedure before taking off and landing, and if he is distracted from doing other things in the process, he may forget which step he has taken in the process, thus missing an important operational step. People who need medication every day are interrupted by other things in their morning (or evening) routines and experience the same problem, and may not remember whether they have taken drugs, which increases their risk of heart attack or death (Nelson et al., 2006).

p39.original: 鉴于前瞻性记忆失败的频率如此之高，我们是否能做些什么来预防它们呢？你觉得呢？
p39.en: Given the frequency of forward-looking memory failures, what can we do to prevent them? What do you think?

p40.original: 专家建议遵循以下步骤来预防前瞻性记忆的遗忘。
p40.en: The experts recommended that the following steps be followed to prevent the oblivion of forward-looking memories.

p41.original: 为自己列一个“要做的事情”清单，并使用其他具体的记忆辅助工具，如手机上的日历或提醒功能。
p41.en: Set yourself a list of “doings to do” and use other specific memory aids such as calendars or alarms on mobile phones.

p42.original: 在进行重要工作时（如学习），不要同时进行多项工作。
p42.en: In the case of important work (e.g. learning), there is no parallel work.

p43.original: 当一项任务很重要时，不要拖延，应当马上去做以免忘记该任务。
p43.en: When a task was important, it should not be delayed, and it should not be forgotten.

p44.original: 使用提醒线索，就像上面例子中的父亲本应做的那样，从而避免忘记一些偏离日常惯例的事情。
p44.en: Use the reminder thread, as the father should have done in the example above, so as not to forget something that deviates from everyday practice.

p45.original: 最后，避免频繁中断。研究还表明，频繁中断或切换任务会增加遗忘当前任务的概率（Finstad et al.，2006）。所以，不要在学习的时候查看手机和社交软件！
p45.en: Finally, frequent interruptions are avoided. The study also shows that frequent interruptions or switchovers increase the probability of forgetting the current task (Finstad et al., 2006). So don't look at your phone and social software while you're studying!

p46.original: 心理学很有用 舌尖现象

p47.original: 请尽可能多地回答以下问题。
p47.en: Please answer as many questions as possible.

p48.original: 在北欧驯鹿被叫作“reindeer”，在北美驯鹿被叫作什么？
p48.en: What is the name of a Nordic reindeer called “reindeer” and of a North American reindeer?

p49.original: 艺术家们把他们用来混合颜料的板子称作什么？
p49.en: What do artists call boards they use to mix paint?

p50.original: 有尖顶的高大的四面石碑叫什么？
p50.en: What's the name of the four tall tablets with their tops?

p51.original: 领航员通过观察星星来确定纬度的仪器是什么？
p51.en: The navigator, by observing the stars, determines what the instrument is for latitude?

p52.original: 用来装剑或匕首的套子叫什么？
p52.en: What's the name of the condom for a sword or dagger?

p53.original: 通常用单桨或单杆就能划动的中式小船叫什么名字？
p53.en: What's the name of a small Chinese boat that usually rows with a single oar or pole?

p54.original: 如果结果如我们所预期的那样，你可能不记得所有的答案，但是你会有一种强烈的感觉，认为自己知道这些问题的答案。你可能会说这些答案“就在嘴边”。心理学家形象地将这种功亏一篑的记忆现象称为舌尖现象（TOT phenomenon）（Brown，1991）。调查显示，大多数人每周都至少有一次“舌尖”（tip-of-the-tongue，TOT）体验。在看《危险边缘》（Jeopardy）知识竞赛的人当中，这种情况可能会发生得更频繁。最近的一项研究还表明，使用手语的聋哑人有时也会有“指尖”（tip-of-the-fingers，TOF）体验，他们确信自己知道一个词，但无法完全提取准确的手语来表达它（Thompson et al.，2005）。显然，在舌尖和指尖现象的背后共同存在着一些基础的记忆加工过程。
p54.en: If the result is as expected, you may not remember all the answers, but you have a strong feeling that you know the answers to those questions. You might say that the answers are “just by the mouth”. Psychologists refer graphically to this loss of memory as the tip of the tongue (TOT phenomenon) (Brown, 1991). The survey shows that most people experience “tip-of-the-tongue” at least once a week. This may happen more frequently among those watching the Jeopardy knowledge contest. A recent study has also shown that deaf and dumb people who use sign language sometimes experience “tip-of-the-fingers” (TOF), who are convinced that they know a word, but are not able to extract the exact sign language to express it (Thompson et al., 2005). It is clear that there are some underlying memory processes behind the tip of the tongue and the tip of the finger.

p55.original: 华盛顿纪念碑是一个顶部呈金字塔尖形状的锥形石碑。你能回忆起我们是如何称呼这种物体的吗？还是会产生舌尖现象呢？
p55.en: The Washington Memorial is a conical stone with the top shape of the pyramid. Can you remember what we call this object? Or do you have a tongue tip?

p56.original: 最常见的舌尖体验集中在对熟人的名字、名人的名字和熟悉的物品的回忆过程中（Brown，1991）。大约在一半情况下，目标词汇最终会在折磨个体一分钟左右后闪现于脑海中（Brown & McNeill，1966）。
p56.en: The most common tipping experience is focused on memories of acquaintances ' names, celebrity names and familiar objects (Brown, 1991). In about half of the cases, the target vocabulary will end up in the mind after about a minute of torture (Brown & McNeill, 1966).

p57.original: 是什么导致了舌尖现象呢？
p57.en: What caused the tip of the tongue?

p58.original: 实验室研究中经常采用的一种可能的解释是背景线索不足。这可能是导致你对上述一些问题感到困惑的原因：我们没有给你足够的背景信息来激活与正确答案相关联的图式。
p58.en: A possible explanation frequently used in laboratory studies is the inadequacy of background leads. This may be the reason why you are confused about some of the above questions: we have not given you enough background information to activate the pattern linked to the right answer.

p59.original: 另一种可能的解释涉及对记忆的干扰：另一个记忆阻碍了当前记忆的通达或提取，就像当你正在想简时意外地遇到了吉尔一样（Schacter，1999）。而且，即使你在上述舌尖现象的演示中无法回忆起某些正确的词汇（北美驯鹿、调色板、方尖碑、六分仪、剑鞘、舢板），你还可以通过再认的方式找到正确答案。尽管你仍不知道要回忆的词本身到底是什么，你也可能会突然想到这些词的一些特征（如“我知道它是以s开头的”）。因此，当提取线索与长时记忆中单词的编码不匹配时，就会出现舌尖现象。
p59.en: Another possible explanation relates to the interference with memory: another memory hinders current memory access or extraction, just as when you are trying to be brief and unexpectedly meet Jill (Schacter, 1999). And even if you cannot recall some of the correct words in the demonstration of the sharpness of your tongue (American reindeer, palettes, tablets, stencils, scorpions, palettes), you can find the right answer by re-recognizing it. While you still don't know what the words are, you may suddenly think of some of the features of those words (e.g. “I know it starts with s”). Therefore, when extracting leads does not match the code of words in long-term memory, a tip of the tongue occurs.

p60.original: 最后，我们敢打赌你说不出七个小矮人的名字。
p60.en: Finally, we bet you can't name the seven dwarfs.
